hello.note: Also heard everywhere: helo. In North Wales: su'mae.

please.note: To a friend or child: os gweli di'n dda. Many speakers just say plîs.

youre_welcome.note: The same word welcomes a guest. Casually also: dim problem.

yes.note: Welsh echoes the verb: ydw (I am), oes (there is), do (past). Ie (North: ia) is for questions not starting with a verb.

no.note: Also echoes the verb: nac ydw (I'm not), nac oes (there isn't), naddo (past).

sorry.note: South Wales: mae'n flin 'da fi — but in the North flin means angry. Casually: sori.

how_are_you.note: Fuller: sut ydych chi? South: shwd ych chi? North: sut dach chi? To a friend: sut wyt ti?

im_fine.note: Also: iawn, diolch. 'Not bad': ddim yn ddrwg.

whats_your_name.note: North Wales: beth ydy'ch enw chi? To a friend: beth yw dy enw di?

my_name_is.note: North Wales: fy enw i ydy Siân. Just as natural: Siân dw i ('I'm Siân').

nice_to_meet_you.note: North Wales: braf cyfarfod â chi. To a friend, say â ti instead of â chi.

where_from.note: To a friend: o ble wyt ti'n dod?

im_from.note: o softens the next word: Cymru → o Gymru, Lloegr → o Loegr.

speak_english.note: Fuller: ydych chi'n siarad Saesneg? Answers: ydw (yes) / nac ydw (no).

dont_understand.note: Spoken: sa i'n deall (South), dw i'm yn dallt (North).

speak_slowly.text: Siaradwch yn arafach, os gwelwch yn dda
speak_slowly.note: Softer as a question: allwch chi siarad yn arafach?

who.note: In Welsh w is often a vowel: pwy sounds like 'pooy'.

how_much.note: North Wales: faint ydy hwn? Also common: faint mae hwn yn gostio?

where_bathroom.note: Tŷ bach is the everyday word; signs usually say toiledau.

can_you_help.note: To a friend: alli di fy helpu i?

what_time.note: North Wales: faint o'r gloch ydy hi?

what_means.text: Beth mae hyn yn ei olygu?
what_means.note: Also common: beth yw ystyr hyn?

two.note: Sounds like 'dye'. Before feminine nouns: dwy (dwy gath, two cats).

five.note: u sounds like the 'i' in 'pin'. Before a noun: pum (pum munud, five minutes).

six.note: ch as in Scottish 'loch'. Before a noun: chwe (chwe diwrnod, six days).

water.note: Long 'oo' and a rolled r. Asking for some: ga i ddŵr, os gwelwch yn dda?

tea.note: Said 'teh'. A cuppa: paned (said panad in the North) or dishgled (South).

im_hungry.note: Colloquially: dw i eisiau bwyd (North: dw i isio bwyd). South also: mae chwant bwyd arna i.

menu_please.text: Ga i'r fwydlen, os gwelwch yn dda?
menu_please.note: Bwydlen (menu) is feminine, so it softens after the: y fwydlen.

bill_please.text: Ga i'r bil, os gwelwch yn dda?
bill_please.note: Ga i …? ('may I have') works for anything: ga i goffi? (coffi softens to goffi).

no_meat.text: Dw i ddim yn bwyta cig
no_meat.note: 'I'm vegetarian': dw i'n llysieuwr (a woman says: llysieuwraig).

enjoy_meal.note: To a friend: mwynha dy fwyd! Often just: mwynhewch!

left.note: 'To the left': i'r chwith. 'On the left': ar y chwith.

right.note: 'To the right': i'r dde. De also means 'south'.

stop_here.text: Stopiwch yma, os gwelwch yn dda
stop_here.note: Colloquially: stopiwch fan hyn (South) or stopiwch fan'ma (North).

want_to_go.note: i softens the place name: Caerdydd → i Gaerdydd, Bangor → i Fangor. North: isio for eisiau.

is_it_far.note: North Wales: ydy o'n bell? Answers: ydy (yes) / nac ydy (no).

one_ticket.text: Un tocyn, os gwelwch yn dda
one_ticket.note: Single: tocyn unffordd. Return: tocyn dwyffordd.

too_expensive.note: Drud (expensive) softens to ddrud after rhy (too).

cheaper.note: South Wales: oes rhywbeth rhatach 'da chi?

id_like_this.text: Ga i hwn, os gwelwch yn dda?
id_like_this.note: More formal: hoffwn i gael hwn, os gwelwch yn dda.

just_looking.note: Very common in shops: jyst edrych, diolch.

pay_card.note: Talu (pay) softens after ga i. Spoken also: gyda cherdyn (South), efo cerdyn (North).

cash.note: In conversation people often just say arian (money) or cash.

big.note: Softens after yn: mae'n fawr (it's big).

small.note: Softens after yn: mae'n fach. Also a warm term of endearment: diolch, bach!

tomorrow.note: Often shortened to fory in speech.

good_evening.note: Not nos da — that is only for bedtime or leaving at night.

see_you_later.note: To a friend: wela i di wedyn. South Wales also: tan toc!

wait_moment.text: Arhoswch funud, os gwelwch yn dda
wait_moment.note: To a friend: aros funud! Casually: eiliad! (one second).

every_day.note: Pob (every) softens to bob in time phrases: bob wythnos (every week).

help.note: A plain "Help!" is also heard, as in English.

dont_feel_well.text: Dw i ddim yn teimlo'n dda

pharmacy.note: In speech many people just say y cemist.

lost_phone.text: Dw i wedi colli fy ffôn
lost_phone.note: Spoken: dw i 'di colli fy ffôn.

allergic.note: i softens the next word: cnau (nuts) → i gnau. South: mae alergedd 'da fi i gnau.

be_careful.note: To a friend: bydd yn ofalus!

dont_know.note: Spoken: sa i'n gwbod (South), dwn i'm (North).

i_like_it.note: Spoken: dw i'n hoffi fe (South), dw i'n licio fo (North).

dont_like_it.text: Dw i ddim yn ei hoffi
dont_like_it.note: Spoken: sa i'n hoffi fe (South), dw i'm yn licio fo (North).

im_tired.note: Worn out: dw i wedi blino'n lân.

welcome.note: Also: croeso i chi! Signs at the border say Croeso i Gymru (Welcome to Wales).

congratulations.note: Stress: llon-guh-var-KHYAH-dye (kh as in 'loch'). For ll, place your tongue for 'l' and blow.

my_family.note: Fy (my) changes teulu to nheulu. In speech people add i: fy nheulu i.

mother.note: Also the word for 'Mum'. Grandma: mam-gu (South), nain (North).

father.note: 'Dad': dad. 'My father': fy nhad. Grandad: tad-cu (South), taid (North).

sister.note: Chw is ch (as in 'loch') + w; in the South often 'hwaer'. 'My sister': fy chwaer.

child.note: Son: mab. Daughter: merch. Children: plant.

friend.note: Used for men and women alike. More formal: cyfaill (a female friend: cyfeilles).

this_is_my_friend.note: Same words for a female friend. In speech often: dyma'n ffrind i.

are_you_married.note: Fuller: ydych chi'n briod? Priod (married) softens to briod after 'n.

have_children.note: South Wales: oes plant 'da chi? Answers: oes (yes) / nac oes (no).

monday.note: Named after the moon (Latin luna); llun alone means 'picture'. 'On Monday': ddydd Llun. 'Monday night': nos Lun.

tuesday.note: Mawrth is Mars (and March). 'Tuesday night': nos Fawrth.

wednesday.note: Mercher is Mercury. 'Wednesday night': nos Fercher.

thursday.note: Iau (Jupiter) sounds like the 'yi' in 'yikes'. 'Thursday night': nos Iau.

friday.note: Gwener is Venus. 'Friday night': nos Wener.

saturday.note: Sadwrn is Saturn. 'Saturday night': nos Sadwrn.

sunday.note: Named after the sun (Latin sol); the sun itself is yr haul. 'Sunday night': nos Sul.

weekend.note: From pen (end) + wythnos (week). 'Have a good weekend!': penwythnos da!

what_day.note: North Wales: pa ddiwrnod ydy hi heddiw? Answer: dydd Llun yw hi.

next_week.note: In speech: wythnos nesa. 'Last week': wythnos ddiwethaf (spoken: wythnos ddwetha).

eleven.note: Literally 'one on ten'. Modern counting: un deg un. Times use un ar ddeg: un ar ddeg o'r gloch.

twelve.note: Literally 'two-ten'. Modern counting: un deg dau.

fifteen.note: Literally 'five-ten'. Modern counting: un deg pump.

twenty.note: Modern counting: dau ddeg. Ugain is usual for ages, money and minutes: ugain munud.

thirty.note: Traditional: deg ar hugain ('ten on twenty'), still heard from older speakers.

fifty.note: Literally 'half a hundred'. Modern counting: pum deg.

hundred.note: Two hundred: dau gant (c softens to g after dau).

thousand.note: Mil is feminine: two thousand is dwy fil, three thousand tair mil.

how_old.note: North Wales: faint ydy'ch oed chi? To a friend: faint yw dy oed di?

years_old.note: The number softens after 'n: tri deg → dw i'n dri deg oed. Ugain stays: dw i'n ugain oed.

red.note: The dragon on the flag is y Ddraig Goch (coch softens to goch).

blue.note: Dark blue: glas tywyll. Light blue: glas golau.

green.note: Softens after yn: mae'n wyrdd (it's green).

yellow.note: Softens after yn: mae'n felyn (it's yellow).

black.note: Sounds like 'dee'. Softens after yn: mae'n ddu (it's black).

white.note: With a feminine noun: gwen (cath wen, a white cat).

what_colour.note: North Wales: pa liw ydy o? Lliw (colour) softens to liw after pa.

this_one.note: With a feminine noun: hon. Also common: yr un yma (spoken: yr un 'ma).

that_one.note: With a feminine noun: honna. Further off: yr un acw (that one over there).

another_one.text: Un arall, os gwelwch yn dda
another_one.note: As a question: ga i un arall? Casually: un arall, plîs.

its_hot.note: Weather is hi (she) in Welsh. South Wales also: mae hi'n dwym.

its_raining.note: North Wales also: mae hi'n glawio. Pouring: mae hi'n bwrw hen wragedd a ffyn ('old women and sticks')!

its_sunny.note: Also: mae'r haul yn tywynnu (the sun is shining).

its_windy.note: Gwyntog softens to wyntog after 'n. Stormy: mae hi'n stormus.

weather_today.note: Also: sut dywydd yw hi heddiw?

beautiful_day.note: Diwrnod softens to ddiwrnod after 'n. Often just: mae'n braf! (it's lovely out).

umbrella.note: Stress the end: um-ba-REL. Often said ambarél.

summer.note: f is said like English v: 'hav'. 'In the summer': yn yr haf.

winter.note: Sounds like 'GUY-av'. 'In the winter': yn y gaeaf.

have_reservation.note: South Wales: mae archeb 'da fi. Also common: dw i wedi bwcio stafell (I've booked a room).

room.note: In speech: stafell. Double room: ystafell ddwbl. Single room: ystafell sengl.

wifi_password.note: North Wales: beth ydy cyfrinair y Wi-Fi? Cyfrinair literally means 'secret word'.

check_out_time.text: Faint o'r gloch mae'n rhaid gadael yr ystafell?
check_out_time.note: Many people just say: faint o'r gloch yw check-out?

map.note: Same word in Welsh. Plural: mapiau.

bus.note: Rhymes with 'puss' — w is a vowel here. Bus stop: safle bws.

next_train.note: In speech: pryd mae'r trên nesa? 'The last train': y trên olaf.

is_this_seat_free.note: Just as natural: oes rhywun yn eistedd yma? (is anyone sitting here?)

what_do_you_do.note: North Wales: beth ydy'ch gwaith chi? To a friend: beth yw dy waith di?

i_work_in.note: Mewn means 'in a': mewn banc, mewn siop. With 'the' or a town use yn: yn y swyddfa, yng Nghaerdydd.

im_student.note: A woman says: dw i'n fyfyrwraig. Myfyriwr (student) softens to fyfyriwr after 'n.

office.note: From swydd (job) + -fa (place). Post office: swyddfa'r post.

meeting.note: 'In a meeting': mewn cyfarfod. In North Wales it also means 'to meet'.

im_busy.note: Prysur softens to brysur after 'n. Very busy: dw i'n brysur iawn.

day_off.note: Also: diwrnod rhydd ('free day'). On holiday: ar wyliau.

colleague.note: A female colleague: cydweithwraig. Plural: cydweithwyr.

lets_start.note: Also: dechreuwn ni! Dechrau softens to ddechrau after i ni.

good_job.note: Literally 'very good'. Warmer: da iawn chi! (to a friend: da iawn ti!). Also: gwych! (brilliant).

table_for_two.text: Bwrdd i ddau, os gwelwch yn dda
table_for_two.note: Dau softens to ddau after i (for). For four: bwrdd i bedwar.

what_recommend.note: North Wales: beth fasech chi'n ei argymell? Simpler: beth sy'n dda yma? (what's good here?)

not_spicy.text: Ddim yn sbeislyd, os gwelwch yn dda
not_spicy.note: Also: ddim yn rhy boeth (not too hot).

vegetarian_food.note: Vegan food: bwyd fegan. Asking: oes gennych chi fwyd llysieuol?

more_water.text: Mwy o ddŵr, os gwelwch yn dda
more_water.note: Mwy o (more) softens the next word: dŵr → ddŵr, bara → fara.

no_sugar.text: Dim siwgr, os gwelwch yn dda
no_sugar.note: With milk: gyda llaeth (South), efo llefrith (North).

im_full.note: Stuffed: dw i'n llawn dop. Politely: dw i wedi cael digon, diolch.

takeaway.text: I fynd, os gwelwch yn dda
takeaway.note: Eating in instead: i fwyta yma.

it_was_delicious.note: North Wales: roedd o'n flasus. Blasus softens to flasus after 'n.

head.note: 'My head': fy mhen. Pen also means 'end', as in penwythnos (weekend).

stomach.note: Tummy or belly: bol (bola in the North).

head_hurts.note: 'I've got a headache': mae pen tost 'da fi (South), mae gen i gur pen (North).

have_fever.note: Gwres means 'heat'. Illnesses go with ar (on): mae annwyd arna i (I've got a cold).

medicine.note: On labels and in pharmacies: meddyginiaeth. North Wales also: ffisig.

dentist.note: From dant (tooth). Toothache: mae'r ddannoedd arna i.

need_rest.note: North Wales: mae angen i mi orffwys. Colloquially: dw i angen gorffwys.

feel_better.note: Much better: dw i'n teimlo'n llawer gwell.

get_well.note: Used in speech and on cards. To a friend also: brysia wella! ('hurry and get better').

lets_meet.note: Literally 'what about meeting'. North Wales: beth am gyfarfod? Over a cuppa: beth am baned?

are_you_free.note: Fuller: ydych chi'n rhydd yfory? To a friend: wyt ti'n rhydd fory?

call_me.note: To a friend: ffonia fi! 'Text me': tecstiwch fi.

your_number.note: North Wales: beth ydy'ch rhif ffôn chi? To a friend: beth yw dy rif ffôn di?

see_you_soon.text: Wela i chi cyn bo hir
see_you_soon.note: To a friend: wela i di cyn bo hir. Also: wela i chi'n fuan.

have_nice_day.note: To a friend: mwynha dy ddiwrnod!

good_luck.note: Also very common: pob hwyl! (all the best).

happy_birthday.note: Adding 'to you': pen-blwydd hapus i chi (to a friend: i ti). Often written penblwydd.

thanks_a_lot.note: Warmer still: diolch yn fawr iawn, or diolch o galon ('from the heart').

miss_you.text: Dw i'n gweld dy eisiau di
miss_you.note: North Wales: dw i'n dy golli di. To more than one person: dw i'n gweld eich eisiau chi.
